evidence.intree_statement: Definition Complete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F.
Definition Cocomplete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F.
Class Limit `(F : J ⟶ C) := { limit_cone : Cone F; ump_limits : ∀ N : Cone F, ∃! u : N ~> limit_cone, ∀ x : J, vertex_map[limit_cone] ∘ u ≈ @vertex_map _ _ _ _ (@coneFrom _ _ _ N) x }.

The definitions below quantify over [∀ (D : Category)] without an explicit smallness hypothesis; the size discipline is instead carried implicitly by the library's universe polymorphism. When [Complete]/[Cocomplete] are instantiated, the universe levels of D become constrained relative to those of C, which is the universe-polymorphic stand-in for "D small relative to C".

statement_record.book: A category C is small-complete (usually just 'complete') when every small diagram in C has a limit — equivalently, when every functor F : J ⟶ C out of a small index category J has a limit in C.
statement_record.intree: Definition Complete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The universal quantification is over all diagram categories D with no explicit smallness side-condition; the library carries that side-condition by universe polymorphism (instantiating Complete constrains D's universes relative to C's), which the file header states verbatim and Adjunction/SAFT.v:138 confirms in a concrete use ('[Complete] forces the diagram category's hom universe to coincide with C's hom universe'). Slightly STRONGER than the propositional reading in one respect: Complete is Type-valued data, a chosen-limit oracle rather than a mere existence claim. Caveat that belongs to Theorem 1, not to this definition: Mac Lane's accompanying announcement that Set, Grp, Ab satisfy completeness is uninstantiated — docs/INHABITATION.md:53 records 'no `Complete`/`Cocomplete` instance exists in-tree'.

statement_record.book: ω denotes the linearly ordered set of all finite ordinals viewed as a category — the free category generated by the infinite chain graph 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → …; diagrams indexed by ω^op are the inverse sequences used throughout the section.
statement_record.intree: [Omega] is the thin category whose objects are the natural numbers and whose morphisms [m ~> n] are proofs of [m ≤ n]. … a functor [Omega ⟶ C] is exactly an ω-indexed diagram [X₀ ~> X₁ ~> X₂ ~> ...] in [C].  (Instance/Omega.v:11–15, with Omega at line 72 and the generating step arrow omega_step at line 85.)
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Mac Lane presents ω as the free category on the chain graph; the library presents it as the thin category of the order ≤ on nat, the standard identification (the free category on a linear chain graph is thin and coincides with the ≤-poset), and supplies the generating step arrow explicitly as omega_step. The order relation is a bespoke Type-valued le_t rather than stdlib's Prop-valued le, deliberately, so that it can eliminate into Type-valued hom-sets — a strengthening, not a weakening. ω^op is available by Construction/Opposite.v; Construction/Chain.v:78 already uses it (Cochain by duality).

statement_record.book: For F : ω^op ⟶ Set with sets F_n and maps f_n : F_{n+1} → F_n, the subset L ⊆ ∏_i F_i of matching strings (f_n x_{n+1} = x_n for all n), with μ_n x = x_n, is a limiting cone; a matching string is exactly a cone from the one-point set, so L = Cone(*, F); and the same recipe works for an arbitrary index category in place of ω^op.
statement_record.intree: Definition end_family : Type := { s : ∀ x : C, F (x, x) & ∀ (x y : C) (f : x ~{C}~> y), fmap[F] (id, f) (s x) ≈ fmap[F] (op f, id) (s y) }  —  with Sets_End : End F proving its universal property.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker. The distinctive technique of the construction — carve the limit out of the product of the family by exactly the compatibility equations, with the equivalence carried pointwise by the setoid rather than by a quotient — is realised in Sets, but only for the END of a mixed-variance functor (the wedge/dinaturality constraint), whose universal property is a wedge UMP, not a cone UMP over a general diagram. No in-tree object is the limit of an ω^op tower of setoids, no indexed product of a family of setoids exists, and Cone(*, F) is never exhibited as a limit apex. Only the finite discrete shapes are instantiated in Sets: Sets_Terminal (Instance/Sets.v:248) and Sets_Cartesian (binary).

statement_record.book: The crux of Theorem 1 is a bijection Cone(X, F) ≅ Set(X, Cone(*, F)) natural in the set X (τ ↦ h with h x = τ·x). Since a J-cone from X is exactly a natural transformation Δ X ⟹ F, this reads Nat(Δ X, F) ≅ Set(X, Cone(*, F)) — an adjunction exhibiting Cone(*, F) as Lim F; so by the very definition of limit, Lim F = Cone(*, F).
statement_record.intree: Proposition LimitIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty C^op (fun c => IsALimit F c) (fun c => @LimitSetoid J C F c)   [= Hom(c, z) ≅ Cone(c, F) naturally], together with  Lemma Cone_Natural_Transform `(F : [J, C]) : ∀ N : C, Δ[J](N) ⟹ F ↔ Cone[N] F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: mixed. The two structural halves of the remark are PRESENT and in greater generality than the book (arbitrary ambient C, not just Set): 'a cone is a natural transformation out of Δ' is Cone_Natural_Transform, and 'being a limit = representing the cone presheaf', i.e. Hom(−, z) ≅ Cone(−, F) naturally, is LimitIsUniversalProperty. What is intree-weaker is precisely the Set-specific payload the remark exists to deliver — that the representing object IS the set of cones out of the point — plus the general adjunction form Δ[J] ⊣ lim, which exists in tree only for J = discrete two (Adjunction/Diagonal/Product.v:36).

gap: Two things missing. evidence.intree_statement: Class CreatesUSplitCoequalizers {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) := { create_coeq {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) (S : SplitCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g)) : ∃ (q : C) (e : y ~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e ∧ (∃ i : @Isomorphism D (U q) (scoeq_obj S), to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S); create_coeq_reflects {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) (S : SplitCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g)) (q : C) (e : y ~> q) (He : e ∘ f ≈ e ∘ g) (i : @Isomorphism D (U q) (scoeq_obj S)) (Hi : to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S) : IsCoequalizer f g q e }.

The second clause is the uniqueness half of creation, phrased in the strongest form the theorem can consume.  Mac Lane's strict definition demands a unique on-the-nose lift of the colimiting cocone and that this lift be colimiting; in a setoid-based library, where downstairs data can only be matched up to isomorphism, the non-evil rendering asks instead that every iso-compatible lift be colimiting.
Definition equivalence_creates_limits {J : Category} (G : J ⟶ C) (L : Limit (F ◯ G)) : Limit G := limit_transport (equivalence_diagram_iso G) (rapl_limit (equiv_adjunction E) (F ◯ G) L).

Class PreservesLimit `(G : J ⟶ C) `(F : C ⟶ D) := { preserves_limit (L : Limit G) : IsALimit (F ◯ G) (F L) }.  (* the file supplies preservation and reflection-of-isos vocabulary only; there is no creation class *)

statement_record.book: V : A ⟶ X creates limits for F : J ⟶ A when (i) for every limiting cone τ : x ⇒ VF in X there is exactly one pair (a, σ) of an object a of A and a cone σ : a ⇒ F with Va = x and Vσ = τ, and (ii) that unique σ is itself a limiting cone in A. Variants by restricting J: creates products (J discrete), creates finite limits (J finite), creates colimits (arrows reversed). Creation says nothing unless VF already has a limit.
statement_record.intree: Class CreatesUSplitCoequalizers {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) := { create_coeq … : ∃ (q : C) (e : y ~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e ∧ (∃ i : U q ≅ scoeq_obj S, to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S); create_coeq_reflects … : IsCoequalizer f g q e }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on three axes. (i) Shape: creation is defined only for coequalizers of U-split parallel pairs, never for limits over a general J, and none of the book's variants (creates products, creates finite limits, creates colimits generally) is defined. (ii) Strictness: the lift is matched to the downstairs datum only up to a packaged comparison isomorphism i with `to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S`, not Mac Lane's on-the-nose `Va = x` and `Vσ = τ`; the file header at :52 acknowledges exactly this deviation, and the uniqueness clause is replaced by the reflection clause (every iso-compatible lift is colimiting), with 'unique up to compatible isomorphism' derived as the corollary create_coeq_unique. (iii) The two limit-side results that carry the word 'creates' — equivalence_creates_limits (Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:486) and the comma development (Construction/Comma/Limit.v:17, 'the projection comma_proj2 creates them') — contain no uniqueness-of-lift clause at all: they are bare lifting maps Limit (F ◯ G) → Limit G / Limit K.
